findings.reason: the section should cite and extend recovery._resolve_commit so the review-record check reuses the resolution semantics check-manifest already applies (abbreviations, {commit} peeling), rather than growing another resolution path that can drift from check-manifest's.
findings.text: §60 asks store_review and check-manifest to validate that reviewed_base_sha/reviewed_head_sha resolve but names no resolver, while recovery._resolve_commit (reckon/crew/recovery.py:378) and its caller _commit_candidates (recovery.py:398) already resolve a named commit against a repository for the manifest commits check-manifest performs (§22, done); a new rev-parse would be the fourth such helper beside it and promotion._resolve_commits (promotion.py:2643)

findings.reason: naming one owner makes both sites call the same resolver, which is exactly the two-readers divergence the plan's own §24/§38/§48 sections repair elsewhere; leaving it implicit re-creates it here.
findings.text: the plan places the "revisions must resolve" rule in store_review (the writer) and in crew check-manifest (the pre-completion check) without naming which owns the rule, so the two refusals can disagree on abbreviation handling or on which repository resolves the id; the resolver that should own it is recovery._resolve_commit, already shared by the manifest-adjacent check

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan's new behaviour lands inside existing deep modules (recovery.py, promotion.py, dispatch.py) behind their existing entries, and §61 is the one move that hides the systemd unit surface behind reckon/service.py rather than adding a parallel class); the sections otherwise consolidate scattered idioms into single helpers (_record_tree §54, one resolver §38, one ok helper §50) rather than adding wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §60's "a review record's revisions must resolve" rule is written to land in two independent sites, store_review (reckon/crew/review.py) and crew check-manifest, with neither the existing resolver nor a single owner named, which is the recurring fork this plan's §61 exists to prevent one layer over.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §60 proposes refusing review records whose revisions do not resolve but cites no existing resolver, though check-manifest already resolves named commits through recovery._commit_candidates/_resolve_commit (and promotion._resolve_commits), the machinery §22 landed for the manifest commits §60 is a third instance of.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the additions that sit over existing machinery carry their extension rationale (the dispatch payload gains the reach rather than a second reservation reader, §43; release reads the wide live claim rather than gaining a parallel checker, §47), and no section adds a layer whose only job is to forward.
